summary.text: The first metamorphic testing approach for query bugs in Datalog engines — cases where evaluating a query returns incorrect results. The authors stress that because Datalog underpins program analyses, such bugs can compromise the soundness of an analysis implemented and formalised in it. Running their tool on three mature engines they found 13 previously unknown query bugs, some deep and revealing critical semantic issues.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: Carries metamorphic testing, established for SQL by SQLancer, into Datalog engines.
supporting_excerpts: The most critical ones manifest as incorrect results when evaluating queries—we refer to these as query bugs.

Given the wide applicability of the language, query bugs may have detrimental consequences, for instance, by compromising the soundness of a program analysis that is implemented and formalized in Datalog.
In this paper, we present the first metamorphic-testing approach for detecting query bugs in Datalog engines.

sources.note: Semantic Scholar records this paper as citing the publication that introduced Pivoted Query Synthesis (PQS), Non-optimizing Reference Engine Construction (NoREC), Ternary Logic Partitioning (TLP).
